text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed higher following a stronger New York market. Near May last traded at $309.00 per tonne, up $3.20. August added $2.50 to close at $308.00 per tonne. Traders said the firm close may encourage some follow through interest on Wednesday but much will depend on whether New York can break through top-of-range resistance above 11.00 cents/lb basis May.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed sharply higher, with the spot May contract ending on the key psychological 11.00 cent mark amid speculative and local buying. There were no fresh fundamental factors behind the rise and it remains to be seen whether the upward momentum can be maintained. Fundamentally at least there is no reason for a significant upswing in world market prices. May added 21 points to close at 11.00 cents/lb, while July closed 14 points higher at 10.72 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 4 and 7 points.

EUROPE - European sugar beet areas received only scattered rains during the week ended April 1 with many locations remaining mainly dry. Plantings are well under way. Soil moisture reserves are still adequate in most areas although showers will be needed over the next month to support germination after below normal receipts last month.

ZIMBABWE - Sugar shipments in 1996/97 (April/March) are lower due to a drought reduced crop which reached no more than 336,700 tonnes, down from 512,000 tonnes attained in 1995/96. Exports in December 1996 amounted to 5,053 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative exports in April/December 1996 up to 144,670 tonnes, down from 154,836 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 189,477 tonnes compared to 233,642 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in April/December 1996 were the European Union with 72,985 tonnes raws compared to 75,688 tonnes, the USA with 36,228 tonnes against 16,100 tonnes and China with 15,000 tonnes against nil. The largest markets for white sugar from Zimbabwe are Botswana with 11,425 tonnes against 13,588 tonnes and Namibia with 8,560 tonnes compared to 12,180 tonnes.

ITALY - Sugar imports in November 1996 amounted to 40,911 tonnes, raw value, up from 32,114 tonnes imported in November 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1996/97 (August/November) up to 134,117 tonnes compared to 94,458 tonnes in August/November 1995. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 379,026 tonnes against 266,279 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in August/November 1996 were Germany with 57,777 tonnes whites against 24,345 tonnes, France with 27,565 tonnes, down from 38,077 tonnes and Brazil with 10,804 tonnes against 2,415 tonnes. Sugar exports in November 1996 amounted to 5,660 tonnes, down from 23,488 tonnes in November 1995. This brought cumulative exports in August/November 1996 up to 54,174 tonnes compared to 129,201 tonnes in the like period the previous year. NORWAY - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 12,813 tonnes against 13,321 tonnes in February 1996. This brought cumulative imports in January/February 1997 up to 24,445 tonnes compared to 25,663 tonnes in January/February 1996. Total imports in 1996 amounted to 188,832 tonnes compared to 173,712 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin in January/February 1997 were Denmark with 11,882 tonnes whites against 16,796 tonnes, the UK with 5,473 tonnes against 5,346 tonnes and Sweden with 3,157 tonnes against nil.
